To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the capacity of broadly neutralizing HIV-1 antibodies to inhibit HIV-1 cell-to-cell transmission varies considerably depending on the epitope targeted by the antibody and the HIV-1 subtype tested.
broadly neutralizing antibodies against HIV-1 are less effective against cell-cell transmitted viruses compared to viruses that are spread as free virus.
the capacity of bnAb to inhibit cell-cell transmission is strain- and epitope-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel HIV-1 entry inhibitors.
understanding the mechanisms that underlie the ability of broadly neutralizing HIV antibodies to inhibit cell-cell spread of HIV-1.
the development of a novel HIV vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the capacity of broadly neutralizing HIV-1 antibodies to block HIV-11 cell-cell transmission is dependent on the strain and epitope specificity of the antibody.
the activity of a given bnAb against cell-cell transmitted virus depends on the virus strain and epitope and the window of action of the bnAb.
the capacity to neutralize HIV prior to CD4 binding is strongly associated with the ability to block free virus transmission but not cell-cell transmission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
broadly neutralizing antibody activity against HIV- 1 cell-cell transmission is strain-dependent and varies with the window of action in the entry process.
the activity of bnAbs is not only dependent on the epitope but also on the mode of HIV-1 transmission.
the potency of bnAbs is not only influenced by their epitopes and neutralization breadth but also the transmission mode and the window of action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the capacity of bnAb to block HIV- 1 cell-cell transmission is strain and epitope-dependent.
the potency of broadly neutralizing antibody (bNAb) activity against HIV- 1 cell-cell transmission is strain-dependent and varies considerably between bNAb-virus combinations.

cell-cell spread of HIV-1 is an important transmission route that can dramatically reduce the potency of neutralizing antibodies and therefore needs to be taken into account when considering the efficacy of antibodies in vivo.
